recipes.name: Venus de Milo Soup
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Cook and stir ground beef in a large pot over medium heat until crumbly and browned, 7 to 10 minutes; drain as much fat from pot as possible. Add onion and garlic to the pot; cook and stir until onion is softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, onion soup mix, bouillon cubes, and bay leaf until well combined; stir in water and mixed vegetables. Increase heat to medium-high; bring to a boil.
Stir in orzo pasta; cook until pasta is tender yet firm to the bite, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Venus de Milo Soup
raw_recipe.description: For this Venus de Milo soup recipe, frozen mixed vegetables, orzo pasta, onion soup mix, and ground beef are simmered in a tomato-flavored broth.

review.reviewBody: I worked at the Venus for years. You forgot three important parts, the mushrooms, the grated Parmesan Romano and the bread for dipping!!!!!
Delicious! I threw in about 1/2 cup of frozen kale and used ground turkey instead of ground beef. It came out yummy and the perfect soup for a cold winter day.

I grew up in Somerset/Swansea, MA near the establishment for which this soup was legendary! And I also spent a couple years working at The Venus de Milo as well. Personally I prefer to omit the mushrooms but they are indeed part of the original recipe. Topping it off with grated Parmesan cheese and served with just the right bread…my preference was always a nice Portuguese stick bread! This recipe is a good version and definitely brings back a lot of fond memories!

I was recently at the Venus for the first time for a lunch and show. I didn't get a chance to purchase the soup there, but this recipe intrigued me. I halved it, and it still makes a lot. I didn't have orzo on hand so I subbed brown basmati rice. Per some of the reviewers, the soup has mushrooms in it, so I did add some along with the onions and garlic. Also had it with some parmesan cheese and wheat French bread and had it a day after I made it for better flavor. A good, hearty soup.

Fantastic soup. I followed the recipe the first time and it was great! The second time I used 1Qt each home made chicken and beef stock in place of the bouillon and water, added 3 more bay leaves, 2 tbs of Worcestershire sauce, some red pepper flake and a full carton of fresh sliced mushrooms. It was even better, but no matter how you slice it this is a great recipe!

This recipe was a great guide. I made a beef bone broth, added fresh celery, onions and carrots. I made small meatballs with the ground beef. Just to add a little more nutrients I added some cabbage. Spices; onion/garlic powder, basil, parsley, salt and pepper. And of course...pasta! Sooooo good!
Made with 4 cups of chicken broth and 4 cups of water instead of onion soup mix, and it was delicious!

I'm not usually a review writer but I feel this recipe is so good that it could use a little extra publicity! I found it when I was looking for a good/quick/easy winter recipe to use up the orzo that had been sitting in the cabinet for a while. Typically I aim for recipes with more reviews but since all the other reviewers raved about it and I happened to have almost all of the ingredients, I decided to give it a try. I was not disappointed. The first time I made the recipe, I followed it exactly and it was fantastic! I made it a second time tonight (perfect for freak April snowstorms in CO), but instead of using beef, I substituted homemade, ground, game sausage. It really made a great soup truly outstanding! As a bonus, the leftovers are really good too. I plan on freezing some this time around so I'm curious to see how it tastes after that considering it has pasta in it. But seeing as how this recipe makes SO much soup, I don't want any to go to waste once the weather warms back up by the end of the week! 

Usually with this type of recipe I would take a lot of liberty, especially in the spice department, but with this one I think it's pretty perfect the way it is! It's got to be something about the combo of the onion soup mix and bouillon gives that gives this recipe a little of that je ne sais quoi factor! Bon Appetite!

This went over very well with my family, even the picky eaters. Added oregano, red pepper flakes, sage, basil, and parsley. Upped bouillon to 3 cubes and garlic to 3 tsp. This makes a LOT of soup, had enough to feed 3 of us, save at least another meal's worth for leftovers in fridge, and freeze another meal's worth as well.

My husband and daughter loved it! Easy, economical and delicious recipe. I used the entire 6 oz of tomato paste because I don't like little bits of leftover stuff, also used 1 1/2 lbs of ground beef because that's how mine is packaged. We will use this recipe a lot in the winter!

Very good and easy version of hamburger soup. I added sliced portobello mushrooms and would have added sliced celery if I had some. You can adjust seasoning. Makes a lot so it stretches that expensive beef. Served with cornbread and sprinkled Parmesan cheese on top.

So my parents actually met at The Venus De Milo almost 60 years ago. I've been making this soup since I got married 30 years ago. It's the best soup beside seafood bisque (we are in new England after all) that I make ! Once you make this it will be in your rotation!

I live in Florida now but I'm from Rhode Island. I've been to the Venus De Milo many times and know how good this soup is but never made. I made it today I had so much soup I ended up giving some to my neighbor. I made my husband and neighbor were very happy, they loved it. Yes it did come out great.
I used to live in Fall River and now I’m 3000 miles away. This is a good recipe that reminds me of my childhood

I I made it according to the directions, however, I used less tomato paste, and I used Knox tomato chicken bouillon and two beef bullion cubes. The soup is really lovely, and the orzo is so nice. Highly recommend.
I make this recipe exactly as the chef wrote it and it comes out perfect every time! So yummy, thanks for sharing!
The restaurant no longer exists so cherish this recipe… This soup is amazing
